steps.title: Design the app and plan how it is built
steps.message:
Use the ui-designer helper to complete DESIGN.md below the closing shipyard:design marker,
following the designing-the-interface skill: the scene, what this must not look like, the
details and wording of each screen. It does not change the generated part, and writes no
screen code.

Then use the architect helper. It already has IDEA.md, reads PROJECT.md, DESIGN.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, and
plans the data and the screens on top of the installed parts and their seams, without
rebuilding anything a part already does. It writes the plan into .shipyard/progress.md as the
"Next" list, one line per step. No code in this step.

steps.title: The first real feature
steps.message:
Phase 1 of 3: The first real feature

One thing, finished properly: the screen first so you can see it, then everything behind it. It tells us the shape of the rest.

When this phase is finished, the person who owns this project should be able
to open the app and see something that was not there before. Please work
towards that rather than towards a complete data model.

This is a working prototype: the main journey has to really work, end to
end, on the real database, with real sign-in where the idea has one.
Sample rows to start from are fine; faking what the journey depends on is not.
Polish, rare cases and nice-to-haves can wait.

This project already has these ready-made parts installed. Use them rather
than writing your own, and do not edit inside their folders:

- **Signing in** — `src/components/auth`
- **The screens people sign in on** — `src/components/auth_screens`
- **A list people can sort and search** — `src/components/data_table`
- **I forgot my password** — `src/components/password_reset`
- **Database foundation** — `src/components/postgres_schema`
- **Emailing your users** — `src/components/transactional_email`
- **The screens every app starts with** — `src/components/ui_blocks`
- **How the app looks** — `src/components/ui_foundation`

If one of them is genuinely wrong for what is being asked, say so rather than
working around it.

Leave the app running at the end. If you cannot, say what is broken rather
than leaving it for the owner to discover.

Use the builder helper for the code and the ui-designer helper for the screens, each screen
against DESIGN.md.

steps.title: Write the browser checks for the core flows
steps.message:
Use the test-engineer helper. Beside e2e/smoke.spec.ts, add or update one Playwright spec per
core flow in IDEA.md and the screens in DESIGN.md: what a person does, step by step, and what
they should see. They run on Shipyard's test copy of the app, which has its own database
(.shipyard/check-server.json), never on the founder's app; do not start a server. Each check
creates the data it needs and never relies on data another check left behind. While you work,
run only the specs you write, one file at a time: npx playwright test e2e/<file>.spec.ts.
Shipyard runs the whole suite when this turn ends. A failing check is a finding: report it, do
not weaken the check.

steps.title: Walk the app in a browser
steps.message:
Use the browser-qa helper. It runs the browser checks one spec file at a time against the app
Shipyard is running, reads the screenshots in test-results/, and reports what is actually on screen, worst first. It
changes nothing. If it finds problems, use the fixer helper for each one, then run the checks
again.

steps.title: Security review
steps.message:
Use the security-reviewer helper on what was built: input validation, what each screen and
route lets a person see and change, secrets, and anything that reads the database. Report
findings in plain words, worst first; use the fixer helper for anything that must change.
